findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the cross-environment verification gap: B2 on the review-bot must verify plan-review attestations via the keyring/era trust-root path (the merge-gate's verify_attestations, opcert.py:246-320) rather than claim_gate_check/plan_review_status (own-principal-only), and re-derive the ACCEPTED/FLAG buckets against THAT surface — otherwise 'foreign_key'/'mismatch'/keyless-host is the expected verdict for a legitimately-reviewed plan and blocking on it inverts the gate.
evidence: attest_gate.py:113 claim_gate_check calls signing.verify_signature against the local env key; :120-125 forwards the raw verdict on the not-verified path
signing.py:401-407 keyless host -> foreign_key for EVERY signature; :410-419 stored_fp != local_fp -> foreign_key; :432-439 HMAC signed-elsewhere -> mismatch

_opcert_signing.py:470-479 op-cert principal != own_principal -> foreign_key WITHOUT invoking the scheme; :481-488 no own pubkey -> foreign_key; comment :386 'a cert for another environment is the merge-gate's job, not the local wrapper's'
opcert.py:246-320 the keyring/era trust-root verification that CAN certify a cross-principal signature is only reached via the merge-gate's verify_attestations path, not claim_gate_check
Live example: ticket 78f1 carries a CERTIFIED op-cert plan-review attestation with principal 'ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5'; on any host whose own principal differs it verifies as foreign_key
Plan FLAG set: '{mismatch, foreign_key, key_not_valid_at_era, invalid, unknown_kind} — tamper/authenticity signals ... must not fail open'
findings.finding: B2's blocking predicate is built on plan_review_status/claim_gate_check, which verifies a plan-review attestation ONLY against the verifying host's OWN environment key. Any attestation signed by a different principal (the normal case for a review-bot host distinct from the developer who ran review-plan) returns verdict 'foreign_key' (HMAC signing.py:401-419; op-cert _opcert_signing.py:470-488) or 'mismatch' (HMAC signed-elsewhere, signing.py:432-439), WITHOUT reaching the cross-environment keyring/era trust-root path (opcert.py:246-320) the merge-gate uses. The plan buckets foreign_key/mismatch as FLAG -> BLOCK. Therefore a legitimately-reviewed, certified oversized bug fix will be BLOCKED on the review-bot host, inverting the gate's purpose.
findings.location: Approach section, B2 verdict-bucket definition (FLAG set includes 'foreign_key'/'mismatch'); Scope 'plan_review_status (attest_gate.py) is read-only/no-LLM, callable from the review-bot checkout'
scenarios: Developer writes fix plan, runs review-plan, gets certified attestation, pushes; review-bot (different environment/principal) runs plan_review_status -> foreign_key -> B2 BLOCKS the compliant change
Review-bot host has no signing key at all -> every attestation verifies foreign_key -> every oversized bug fix blocked regardless of review state
findings.suggested_fix: Read the attestation through the same cross-host trust root the Gerrit merge-gate already uses (era-valid keyring verification), so a plan reviewed in a different environment reads as certified; keep 'foreign_key'/'mismatch' in FLAG only for the keyring-verified surface. Re-bucket keyless-host/no-trust-root outcomes into INFRA-FAIL-OPEN (advisory), and add an integration test where the fixture attestation's principal differs from the review-bot's own principal to prove a certified cross-host plan is ACCEPTED, not blocked.

findings.finding: B2's 'review-bot DET criterion' with its bespoke ACCEPTED/FLAG/INFRA-FAIL-OPEN verdict predicate does not reference the code-review gate's EXISTING data-driven DET-criterion framework, which already generalizes exactly this fail-open-vs-block distinction. code_review/registry.det_criteria() + criterion_for_detector() route exec:"DET" entries carrying a per-criterion fail_mode ('open'|'closed', ADR 0016), and code_review/detectors.apply_failclosed() is the consumer-side verdict mutator that BLOCKs a MATCH per blocking_enabled while an ABSTAIN only blocks when fail_mode=='closed' (else recorded as coverage, never blocks) — the same open/closed axis B2 re-invents as INFRA-FAIL-OPEN (never block) vs FLAG (block). The plan should confirm whether B2's criterion rides this existing routing/fail_mode/apply_failclosed path (adding a DET routing entry + a predicate) or deliberately builds a parallel mechanism, and justify a parallel build if chosen (B2's predicate keys on ticket type + diff line count + attestation verdict rather than an engine_b detector over changed files, so a full run_detectors fit is not obvious).
findings.location: Approach §B2 ('DET code-review criterion at Gerrit'; review-bot DET criterion) + Scope bullet 'review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to B2 committing to one of: (a) express the bug-size check as a code_review DET criterion (routing entry with fail_mode, verdict adjustment via apply_failclosed), reusing the established MATCH=block / fail_mode-open=advisory semantics; or (b) explicitly note it is a distinct non-detector predicate that cannot ride run_detectors, and reuse apply_failclosed's fail-open/block posture rather than re-implementing verdict mutation.
